summary: Rear range light on Caraquet Bay, New Brunswick: a Coast Guard skeletal tower of 1978, wrapped in wood in 1991, deactivated in 2020.

structures.note: Coast Guard skeletal range tower of 1978; wooden siding added by the city in 1991. The 13 m height is the wrapped tower as the Lighthouse Directory describes it.

facts.ownership: Disputed: the Lighthouse Directory gives the Canadian Coast Guard as owner and the Ville de Caraquet as site manager; LighthouseFriends says the City of Caraquet owns it.

events.note: Coast Guard skeletal rear range tower
City added wooden siding to the skeletal tower and made it the centrepiece of a town park
Town restored and renovated the tower with its present white and blue colour scheme
Range deactivated September 2020; the tower still carries the red range daymark

notes_for_editor: Evidence is thin and rests on two web directories (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett) that agree on the 1978 skeletal tower, the 1991 wrapper and the 2020 deactivation. No primary source was found for the 1978 installation, and the 2019 restoration and the front light come from Rowlett alone. Two disputes stand: (1) ownership (Rowlett: Canadian Coast Guard owner, Ville de Caraquet site manager; LighthouseFriends: City of Caraquet owns it); (2) the record's other name 'Caraquet' and the 1903 range: LighthouseFriends ID 1224 and the 1903 Marine report place Caraquet's first range towers at Lower Caraquet, now the Town of Bas-Caraquet, a separate station that this batch did not cover. The sources do not say whether the 1978 Pointe a Brideau range replaced or sat on the same line as the 1903 pair, so the story does not link them. Check whether the Bas-Caraquet pair needs its own record. The 1903 Marine report page was read from its OCR text and printed p. 66 is confirmed by the archive's page index. The Canadian Coast Guard New Brunswick List of Lights entry (A1319.3) was not read, so the status rests on Rowlett. Wikidata, Wikimedia Commons and ARLHS CAN-895 were not read. Travel listings (Expedia, Evendo, MindTrip) say 'constructed in the 19th century' for this tower; they contradict the two directories and were not used. LighthouseFriends' cached page shows a broken character for the accent in 'Pointe à Brideau', so the evidence quote keeps that character as cached. The record's access level and visit fields were updated from 'unknown' to 'grounds open, tower closed'. The 1903 Marine report (fiscal year labelled 1903, Sessional Paper 21) is cited for the Lower Caraquet range lighting of 24 September 1903, a date after its fiscal year-end, so the report was written later and records the event as dated; the date is taken as the event's own date. The parallel record ca-nb-caraquet-range-front (same batch, another agent) covers the Bas-Caraquet pair and agrees that the Pointe a Brideau range is a different station; check that the record's other name 'Caraquet' is not confused with it.
